# noised-lmots

[![crates.io noised-lmots](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/noised-lmots.svg?label=noised-lmots)](https://crates.io/crates/noised-lmots) [![docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/noised-lmots)](https://docs.rs/noised-lmots) [![CI](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/LICENSE)
<!-- repo-config:badges:end -->

Hash-based post-quantum signatures for Solana programs and clients, from [RFC 8554](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8554):

- **LM-OTS** `LMOTS_SHA256_N32_W4` (typecode 3): one-time signatures. The [Noised](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised) post-quantum vault signs each withdrawal with one of these keys and rotates to the next in the same instruction.
- **LMS** `LMS_SHA256_M32_H10` (typecode 6) over that LM-OTS: 1,024 one-time leaves under one 56-byte public key. A Noised creator identity is one LMS key; the launchpad program verifies its signature on-chain before a launch can go live, and before every Autopilot change.

Both rest only on SHA-256, so a quantum computer gains at most Grover's square-root speed-up against them: about 128-bit security against quantum attackers. The crate is `no_std` (with `alloc`), has no `unsafe` code, and takes SHA-256 as a trait, so on-chain it uses the `sol_sha256` syscall and off-chain any implementation.

> **Status: pre-audit, not yet on crates.io.** No independent audit has been completed; the crate has had internal reviews (by AI agents, [docs/AUDIT.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/AUDIT.md)) and none of them found an issue in its verification code. Its first crates.io release is **coming soon**; until then, depend on it by git (below). The parameter sets are the ones RFC 8554 defines and NIST SP 800-208 lists, but this crate carries no NIST approval: Noised's keys are software keys derived from a recovery phrase or a passkey secret, which SP 800-208 does not allow.

## Install

Once it is on crates.io:

```sh
cargo add noised-lmots                                  # verification only: what an on-chain program needs
cargo add noised-lmots --features signer,sha2-backend   # clients: key generation, signing, a SHA-256 backend
```

Until then, from this repository (pin a commit you reviewed):

```toml
[dependencies]
noised-lmots = { git = "https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised", rev = "<commit>" }
# clients: noised-lmots = { git = "https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised", rev = "<commit>", features = ["signer", "sha2-backend"] }
```

Releases are published from this repository's release workflow through crates.io trusted publishing. The published crate contains the library only (`src/`, this README, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`); the RFC 8554 known-answer tests, the benchmark and the mutation check stay in the repository.

## Features

| Feature | Adds |
|---|---|
| (none) | Verification only: `verify` (LM-OTS), `candidate_public_key`, `key_id`, `lms_verify`, `identity_id`, strict key and signature parsing (`LmsPublicKey`, `LmsSignature`), the constants. This is what an on-chain program needs. |
| `signer` | Key generation and signing (RFC 8554 Appendix A key derivation): `PrivateKey` (`public_key`, `randomizer`, `sign`, `sign_deterministic`), `LmsPrivateKey` (`derive_identity`, `leaf`, `keygen`), `LmsKeyPair` (`public_key`, `identity_id`, `nodes`, `auth_path`, `sign`, `sign_deterministic`), `hmac_sha256`. |
| `sha2-backend` | `Sha2`, a SHA-256 backend on the `sha2` crate, for clients and tests. |

The only dependency is `sha2` 0.10 (optional, without default features).

## Use it on-chain: verification

Verification needs no feature. Give it the runtime's SHA-256 syscall (here through `solana-sha256-hasher`):

```rust
use noised_lmots::{identity_id, lms_verify, Sha256};

struct SolSha256;
impl Sha256 for SolSha256 {
    fn hashv(parts: &[&[u8]]) -> [u8; 32] {
        solana_sha256_hasher::hashv(parts).to_bytes()
    }
}

/// The leaf a creator identity's signature used, if it is valid and by the expected identity.
fn check(lms_pk: &[u8; 56], message: &[u8], lms_sig: &[u8], expected_identity: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<u32> {
    if identity_id::<SolSha256>(lms_pk) != *expected_identity {
        return None; // SHA256(0x21 || public key) is the launch's `pq_identity`
    }
    lms_verify::<SolSha256>(lms_pk, message, lms_sig) // Some(q), q < 1024, read from the signature
}
```

This is what the Noised launchpad does in `attest_launch` and `pq_authorize`: it verifies the signature, then marks leaf `q` used in the identity's on-chain bitmap so that no leaf is ever accepted twice. The vault does the same with `verify` for a standalone LM-OTS key.

## Use it off-chain: an LMS identity

With the features `signer` and `sha2-backend`:

```rust
use noised_lmots::{identity_id, lms_verify, LmsPrivateKey, LmsPublicKey, LmsSignature, Sha2, LMS_SIG_LEN};

let master = [7u8; 64]; // the post-quantum phrase's 64-byte BIP-39 seed (never a wallet key)
let key = LmsPrivateKey::derive_identity::<Sha2>(&master, 1, 0) // cluster byte 1 = devnet, identity 0
    .expect("cluster <= 2 and a non-zero master");
let pair = key.keygen::<Sha2>(); // the whole tree: about 1.14 million SHA-256 compressions
let pk: [u8; 56] = pair.public_key().to_bytes();

// The launch's `pq_identity` and the seed of its on-chain Identity account.
let pq_identity: [u8; 32] = identity_id::<Sha2>(&pk);
assert_eq!(pq_identity, pair.identity_id::<Sha2>());

// Leaf 5 signs this message and nothing else, ever.
let sig = pair.sign_deterministic::<Sha2>(5, b"attestation message").expect("q < 1024");
assert_eq!(sig.len(), LMS_SIG_LEN); // 2,508 bytes
assert_eq!(LmsSignature::parse(&sig).map(|s| s.q), Some(5));

// Verification returns the leaf the signature used (read from the signature itself).
assert_eq!(lms_verify::<Sha2>(&pk, b"attestation message", &sig), Some(5));
assert_eq!(lms_verify::<Sha2>(&pk, b"another message", &sig), None);

// Strict parsing: anything but this parameter set is refused.
assert!(LmsPublicKey::from_bytes(&pk).is_some());
assert!(LmsPublicKey::from_bytes(&pk[..55]).is_none());
```

`derive_identity` is the derivation every Noised client uses (the TypeScript SDK byte for byte):

```text
path = cluster (0 mainnet, 1 devnet, 2 localnet) || u32le(identity_index)
SEED = SHA256("phalanx/pq/identity/v1/seed" || master || path)
I    = SHA256("phalanx/pq/identity/v1/id"   || master || path)[..16]
```

The cluster byte keeps each cluster's leaves apart, because the program cannot see which cluster it runs on. The domain tags keep the project's earlier name on purpose: changing a tag would change every key derived from a phrase or passkey.

## Use it off-chain: a standalone LM-OTS key (the vault)

```rust
use noised_lmots::{key_id, verify, PrivateKey, Sha2, SIG_LEN};

// A vault key: identifier I, leaf index q (the vault's sequence) and secret SEED.
// (The SDK derives all three from the 24-word phrase; fixed bytes here.)
let key = PrivateKey { id: [0x22; 16], q: 7, seed: [0x11; 32] };
let pk = key.public_key::<Sha2>(); // 67 hash chains of 15 steps each

let message = b"withdraw 1,000,000 base units to <recipient>";
let mut sig = [0u8; SIG_LEN]; // 2,176 bytes: C || y[0..67]
assert!(key.sign_deterministic::<Sha2>(message, &mut sig));

assert!(verify::<Sha2>(&pk, message, &sig));
assert!(!verify::<Sha2>(&pk, b"another message", &sig));

// Signing the same message again reproduces the same bytes: a retry is not a second signature.
let mut again = [0u8; SIG_LEN];
assert!(key.sign_deterministic::<Sha2>(message, &mut again));
assert_eq!(sig, again);

// The 32-byte name the vault program uses as a PDA seed: SHA256(0x20 || public key).
let seed: [u8; 32] = key_id::<Sha2>(&pk);

// The deterministic randomizer's known answer (SPEC §3.10): every signer must reproduce it.
let c = PrivateKey { id: [0x22; 16], q: 7, seed: [0x11; 32] }.randomizer::<Sha2>(b"phalanx");
let hex: String = c.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
assert_eq!(hex, "efff9f338802ed72a95c53d848647c110c67a6a943e9aeecf572bd978e9d79d3");
```

Every snippet in this README was compiled and run against this crate's source before release.

## One-time keys: the rule that matters

**Each LM-OTS key, and each LMS leaf, may sign at most one message, ever.** Two signatures from one key, even of the same message under another randomizer `C`, reveal enough hash-chain values for anyone to forge signatures with that key. Re-broadcasting the same signature is fine.

To make retries safe, `sign_deterministic` derives the randomizer as `HMAC-SHA256(SEED, "phalanx/pq/lmots/C" || I || u32str(q) || message)` (the construction FIPS 205 uses for SLH-DSA's `PRF_msg`): signing the same message again with the same key gives the same bytes. The crate does not track which leaves were used. The caller must record every leaf durably **before** releasing its signature, and must treat a signature as used once it was revealed in any way (sent, simulated or stored), even if it never landed: the TypeScript SDK's leaf and vault-key ledgers do exactly this, and the Noised launchpad and vault also refuse a second signature at a leaf on-chain.

`LmsKeyPair::sign` and `sign_deterministic` verify the signature against the public key before returning it, so a faulty tree never produces an invalid signature.

## API

Always available (verification):

| Item | What |
|---|---|
| `trait Sha256 { fn hashv(parts: &[&[u8]]) -> [u8; 32]; }` | The SHA-256 backend: `sol_sha256` on-chain, anything off-chain. |
| `verify::<H>(pk: &PublicKey, msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> bool` | LM-OTS verification (RFC 8554 Algorithm 4b), constant-time comparison. |
| `candidate_public_key::<H>(id, q, msg, sig) -> Option<[u8; 32]>` | The public key hash `Kc` a signature implies (`None` for a wrong length). |
| `key_id::<H>(pk: &PublicKey) -> [u8; 32]` | `SHA256(0x20 || public key)`: the vault's PDA seed for a key. |
| `PublicKey { id, q, k }`, `PublicKey::to_bytes() -> [u8; 56]` | An LM-OTS public key: `u32str(3) || I || u32str(q) || K`. |
| `lms_verify::<H>(pk: &[u8; 56], msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> Option<u32>` | LMS verification (RFC 8554 Algorithms 6 and 6a, every length and typecode fixed); returns the leaf `q`. `#[must_use]`. |
| `identity_id::<H>(pk: &[u8; 56]) -> [u8; 32]` | `SHA256(0x21 || public key)`: a creator identity's on-chain name. |
| `LmsPublicKey::{from_bytes, to_bytes}`, `LmsSignature::parse` | Strict parsers: exactly this parameter set, `q < 1024`. |
| Constants | `TYPECODE` 3, `N` 32, `W` 4, `P` 67, `LS` 4, `ID_LEN` 16, `SIG_LEN` 2,176, `PUBLIC_KEY_LEN` 56, `CHAIN_END` 15, `D_PBLC`, `D_MESG`, `DOMAIN_KEY_ID` 0x20; `LMS_TYPE` 6, `LMS_OTS_TYPE` 3, `LMS_HEIGHT` 10, `LMS_LEAVES` 1,024, `LMS_TREE_NODES` 2,047, `LMS_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN` 56, `LMS_SIG_LEN` 2,508, `D_LEAF`, `D_INTR`, `DOMAIN_IDENTITY_ID` 0x21, `RANDOMIZER_TAG`. |

With `signer`:

| Item | What |
|---|---|
| `PrivateKey { id, q, seed }` | An LM-OTS private key (RFC 8554 Appendix A secrets). `public_key::<H>()`, `randomizer::<H>(msg)`, `sign_deterministic::<H>(msg, out) -> bool`, `sign::<H>(msg, c, out) -> bool` (caller-supplied randomizer; prefer the deterministic one). |
| `LmsPrivateKey { seed, id }` | `derive_identity::<H>(master: &[u8; 64], cluster: u8, identity_index: u32) -> Option<Self>` (`None` for a cluster above 2 or an all-zero master), `leaf(q) -> Option<PrivateKey>`, `keygen::<H>() -> LmsKeyPair`. |
| `LmsKeyPair` | `public_key()`, `identity_id::<H>()`, `private_key()`, `nodes()` (the 2,047 public node hashes), `auth_path(q)`, `sign::<H>(q, msg, c) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`, `sign_deterministic::<H>(q, msg) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`. |
| `hmac_sha256::<H>(key, parts) -> [u8; 32]` | RFC 2104 HMAC for keys of at most one block. |
| `IDENTITY_SEED_TAG`, `IDENTITY_ID_TAG`, `MAX_IDENTITY_CLUSTER` | The identity derivation's tags and the largest cluster byte (2). |

With `sha2-backend`: `Sha2`, which implements `Sha256`.

The full documentation is on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/noised-lmots) once the crate is published, and in the source ([`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/crates/noised-lmots/src/lib.rs), [`src/lms.rs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/crates/noised-lmots/src/lms.rs)).

## Formats

```text
LM-OTS signature = C (32) || y[0..67] (67 × 32)                                  2,176 bytes (typecode implied)
LM-OTS public key = u32str(3) || I (16) || u32str(q) || K (32)                    56 bytes
LMS public key   = u32str(6) || u32str(3) || I (16) || T[1] (32)                 56 bytes
LMS signature    = u32str(q) || u32str(3) || C || y[0..67] || u32str(6) || path[0..10] (10 × 32)   2,508 bytes
                   offsets: q 0..4 | LM-OTS type 4..8 | C 8..40 | y 40..2184 | LMS type 2184..2188 | path 2188..2508
leaf             T[r] = SHA256(I || u32str(r) || 0x8282 || K_q)                  r = 1024 + q
interior         T[r] = SHA256(I || u32str(r) || 0x8383 || T[2r] || T[2r+1])   1 <= r < 1024
key id           SHA256(0x20 || LM-OTS public key)
identity id      SHA256(0x21 || LMS public key)
```

Every hash is tweaked with the key identifier `I`, the leaf index `q` and the chain position, as RFC 8554 specifies, which rules out multi-target attacks. The module documentation has the complete byte layout and the registry of domain bytes (0x20, 0x21; new Noised domains take the next free value).

## Cost

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| `lms_verify` on SBF (SBPF v3 release build, LiteSVM 0.17, Agave 4.3 cost model, 129 signatures of 173-byte messages) | `8,674 + 137 × steps` CU: about 78k on average, 91k at the 99th percentile, 144k for the worst digest any signature can have |
| RFC 8554 Test Case 2 verified on-chain | 80,563 CU (525 chain steps) |
| The launchpad's whole `attest_launch` (signature, leaf bitmap, account writes) | 79,772 to 114,476 CU over all 1,024 leaves of one identity; 170k projected for the worst case |
| Host, Ryzen 7 5800X, `sha2` backend, release build (`examples/lms_bench.rs`) | key generation 62 ms, signing 65 µs (with self-verification), verification 31 µs |

`steps` is the number of Winternitz chain steps a verification walks (`sum(15 - digit)` over the 67 chains: about 506 on average, 990 at most). Source: [docs/evidence/2026-10-09-lms-cost-measurements.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/evidence/2026-10-09-lms-cost-measurements.md). An LMS signature does not fit a legacy 1,232-byte transaction; Noised sends it in a v1 transaction (SIMD-0385, up to 4,096 bytes).

## `no_std` notes

- `#![no_std]` with `extern crate alloc`: the crate needs an allocator (every Solana program has one). The LM-OTS verification path allocates one 2,144-byte buffer; key generation (feature `signer`) allocates the tree.
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- No randomness and no clock: signing is deterministic, and key derivation takes the caller's 64-byte master.
- SHA-256 is the caller's (`Sha256` trait), so the crate never pulls a hash implementation into an on-chain program unless `sha2-backend` is enabled.

## Test vectors and tests

In the repository, not in the published crate:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| RFC 8554 Appendix F, Test Cases 1 and 2 as the appendix prints them, and Test Case 2's top-level tree (`LMS_SHA256_M32_H10` over `LMOTS_SHA256_N32_W4`, the parameter set this crate implements), as JSON | [`tests/rfc8554_appendix_f.json`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/crates/noised-lmots/tests/rfc8554_appendix_f.json), [`tests/rfc8554_tc2.json`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/crates/noised-lmots/tests/rfc8554_tc2.json) |
| LM-OTS and LMS known-answer, tamper, length and every-leaf tests | [`tests/lmots.rs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/crates/noised-lmots/tests/lmots.rs), [`tests/lms.rs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/crates/noised-lmots/tests/lms.rs) |
| Cross-language vectors (vault withdrawals, identities and attestations) shared with the TypeScript SDK | [`tests/integration/vectors/`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/tree/main/tests/integration/vectors) |
| An independent standard-library Python implementation that re-derives the Appendix F vectors and the attestation vectors | [`scripts/pq/lms_reference.py`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/scripts/pq/lms_reference.py) |
| The mutation check (31 of 31 mutants killed) | [`scripts/pq/lms_mutants.py`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/scripts/pq/lms_mutants.py) |

```sh
cargo test -p noised-lmots --features signer,sha2-backend      # 35 tests: unit, RFC 8554 Appendix F, RFC 4231 HMAC, the randomizer's known answer
python3 -I scripts/pq/lms_reference.py appendix-f crates/noised-lmots/tests/rfc8554_appendix_f.json
cargo run --release -p noised-lmots --features signer,sha2-backend --example lms_bench   # host timings and the syscall CU model
```

The Test Case 2 tests regenerate the published public key from its seed, verify the published signature at leaf 3 and reproduce that signature byte for byte; the Python reference re-derives both test cases of the appendix independently. The TypeScript SDK (`@noisedlabs/sdk`) is tested byte for byte against this crate.
